answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with random-walk trust from seed havens: standing flows outward from a few established seeds along real interaction edges, like light through a prism splitting into paths that only reach genuinely connected identities. A farm cluster has few true edges to the seeds, so its random walks rarely land there, and buying many genuine edges costs real history per fake. One honest agent needs only one real link to a haven, and its trust arrives like a comet: fast, verifiable, and hard to forge in bulk.
